tasks.title: Fence collector ownership and keep leases alive during slow or empty runs
tasks.goal: I want you to make collection safe when a worker stalls, crashes, receives no usable records, or loses its lease to another worker.
tasks.context: collection_health.py has a 30-minute source lease and worker.py renews it only when a record is yielded. Inspect and reproduce the consequences before changing behavior. A stale worker must not keep writing after a replacement starts.
requirements: Use the existing run/lease ID as a fencing token. Heartbeat and finish must update only the currently owned lease, with atomic database predicates. Renew on elapsed time while discovering, pacing and fetching, not only when a valid advert is emitted.

Use one cooperative heartbeat mechanism with an injected clock/scheduler for tests. Set a documented interval no greater than 60 seconds, comfortably below the lease duration; do not spawn an unbounded thread per URL.

Check ownership before each new outbound request and before committing an observation. If lease ownership is lost, stop that run, classify it as interrupted/lease_lost and preserve the replacement’s state.
Keep provider pacing global within one leased provider even when cities differ. Preserve independent concurrency across Otodom, Gratka and Morizon; do not increase source request budgets.
A stale completion may finalize its own historical run as interrupted, but must not clear the new owner’s lease, retry-after, failure count or success timestamp.

Test PostgreSQL with two separate sessions/processes and deterministic synchronization barriers, not only SQLite or arbitrary sleeps. Leave cloud coordination unchanged and explicitly documented until a cloud-specific contract is implemented.

An HTTP request already in flight when ownership changes may still complete; fence its result at commit time. Do not promise network-level cancellation or atomicity between a SQL lease check and an external HTTP server.

acs.text: Only one worker owns a provider’s collection lease at a time.
A run taking longer than one lease duration with zero emitted records remains owned while heartbeats succeed.
After detected lease loss the worker starts no new requests; after takeover no observation can commit under the old token, including results from an already in-flight request.
Finishing the old run cannot change the replacement’s lease or health state.
Kraków and Warszawa health remain distinguishable while sharing the provider request budget.
Interruption/restart does not create duplicate observations, alerts or inactive status from transport failure.

tests.given: Two PostgreSQL workers claim the same provider simultaneously
tests.then: Exactly one owns the lease; the other reports already_running.

tests.given: A fake clock and a discovery stream with no valid records
tests.when: Advance beyond 30 minutes while heartbeat callbacks run
tests.then: Lease stays current; run is not falsely interrupted.

tests.given: Worker A stalls, its lease expires, and worker B claims
tests.then: A's late result/finish is fenced and it starts no new request after detecting loss; B's ID, retry state and last-success remain unchanged.

tests.given: Kraków run expires and Warszawa replacement is active
tests.then: Old run reports interrupted; replacement reports running.

tests.given: A worker crashes after committing one observation
tests.when: Restart and replay the same observation
tests.then: Receipt/history/canonical data remain idempotent; no new notification.

tests.given: Heartbeat database write fails while a request is pacing
tests.when: Advance to the next request boundary
tests.then: Run stops safely and exposes a bounded diagnostic; no false delisting.

deliverables: Reproduction tests and fix
Documented lease state transitions and restart command
PostgreSQL race-test evidence
non_goals: No provider concurrency increase, anti-bot workaround or cloud scheduler deployment.
Do not treat source disappearance or HTTP errors as removal.

tasks.title: Reduce download volume with conditional requests and bounded retries
tasks.goal: I want you to reduce unnecessary listing downloads while preserving accurate freshness, price history and source-specific request limits.
tasks.context: The collector already skips fresh records and keeps one unchanged daily checkpoint. It does not retain HTTP validators or Retry-After timing. A 304 response must only reuse a known valid representation, never invent a listing.
write: backend/realtoruch/migrations.py (additive SQLite upgrade for this task only)
requirements: Persist ETag/Last-Modified and representation provenance privately per source plus canonical URL. Bound stored header lengths; do not persist Authorization, cookies or raw phone numbers. Use reserved migration 005 for rental state if needed.

Send If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since only for the same source URL with a previously validated payload. A 304 may advance checked freshness using that payload while unchanged-history limits and no-alert rules still apply.
For an orphan 304, make at most one unconditional retry inside the existing budget; if it still cannot be interpreted, report an error and leave canonical state unchanged.

Honor Retry-After delta seconds and HTTP-date for 429/503. Persist the defer time and exit the source; do not sleep a worker indefinitely or retry a 403. On timeouts/502, allow at most two bounded attempts with jitter, retaining provider pacing.
Account for every network attempt, including robots, retries and conditional requests, in run telemetry. Preserve the 5 MB page cap, HTTPS allowlist, redirect rejection and robots semantics.
Define cloud state payload compatibility with optional validator fields and fake-client tests only. Do not change the live enabled-source set or apply infrastructure.

Implement fresh-schema and existing-database upgrades for both PostgreSQL and SQLite through T01's migration contract. Register only this task's reserved version(s), preserve applied migrations/checksums and prove existing rows retain their values. Coordinate the shared registry/upgrade file with the integrator.

acs.text: Unchanged supported pages transfer no body after a valid cached validator exists.
A 304 cannot create a new home or restore previously invalid/missing payloads.
Freshness advances without extra same-day unchanged history or notifications.
429/503 backoff survives process restart; 403 stops without retry loops.
Retries never exceed the declared per-source request rate or attempt cap.
Legacy SQL/Bigtable payloads without validators remain readable and public responses expose no validator/credential metadata.

tasks.title: Make search indexing monotonic, batched and safe under retries
tasks.goal: I want you to prevent an older indexing attempt from restoring stale prices or active status, and reduce indexing round trips without losing updates.
tasks.context: worker.index_once reads canonical rows and writes documents one by one while its transaction owns outbox rows. The deployment currently requires one indexer. Add a verified ordering contract before allowing more than one worker.
write: backend/realtoruch/migrations.py (additive SQLite upgrade for this task only)
requirements: Introduce a positive monotonic canonical search revision assigned in the same SQL transaction as every public-document change. Cover ingestion, moderation, merge/split, account withdrawal and advertiser-profile changes; never use wall-clock timestamps as version counters.

Use bounded Elasticsearch bulk requests (default <=100 documents and <=5 MiB encoded payload). Inspect each item, not only the HTTP status. Batch-load source/profile data to avoid per-document query multiplication.

Use strict external versioning for document writes, verified against the installed Elasticsearch 8.19.6 server. Treat a version conflict as acknowledged only when the stored version is equal/newer; never use external_gte to overwrite equal revisions with different content.

Claim work with short SQL transactions and fencing/lease ownership as needed. Send network requests outside long-held canonical locks; acknowledge only revisions that were actually sent or superseded. A newer pending revision must remain pending.
Keep inactive/hidden alias tombstone documents with a newer revision so replay cannot resurrect discovery entries. Avoid deleting version evidence prematurely.

Provide a local rebuild command that populates a new index, checks counts/sample versions and switches an alias only after validation. Keep the current single-indexer deployment default until concurrency tests pass; no cloud reindex is executed.

Implement fresh-schema and existing-database upgrades for both PostgreSQL and SQLite through T01's migration contract. Register only this task's reserved version(s), preserve applied migrations/checksums and prove existing rows retain their values. Coordinate the shared registry/upgrade file with the integrator.

Measure healthy local index convergence after a committed batch of 100 changed homes: all expected revisions should be visible within 30 seconds on the declared four-core/8-GiB benchmark profile. Record the polling/refresh configuration and report an unmet target; never hide lag by returning a fabricated zero.

acs.text: Older or duplicate writes never overwrite a newer indexed price/status.
Ingestion during an in-flight index request leaves the newer revision queued and eventually searchable.
Mixed-success bulk responses acknowledge successes only; retryable failures remain retryable.
Two indexers do not lose updates or resurrect hidden/delisted/merged homes.
Public indexed payloads contain only approved fields; profile changes produce a revision update.
The rebuild command can fail before alias switch without disrupting the existing index and can rebuild after a reset.
A healthy local batch of 100 committed changed homes reaches all expected search revisions within the declared 30-second convergence target.

tests.then: Search remains 4,200; conflicts are handled without overwriting.

tests.then: 12 acknowledgement cannot consume 13; second pass indexes 13.

tests.then: Each item receives the correct persisted status; no blanket success.

tests.then: Latest hidden/inactive state wins; no active result after convergence.

tests.then: Original alias remains usable until fully validated replacement succeeds.

tests.given: Healthy local SQL/Elasticsearch and 100 committed changed homes
tests.when: Run indexing with the documented polling/refresh settings
tests.then: All expected revisions become visible within 30 seconds; otherwise AC07 is recorded as failed, with measured lag retained.

deliverables: Revision migration, indexer implementation and rebuild command

No arbitrary public Elasticsearch DSL or port-9200 exposure.

tasks.title: Create a labelled duplicate-identity evaluation dataset
tasks.goal: I want you to measure duplicate matching against explicit positive, negative and ambiguous examples before anyone changes matching thresholds.
tasks.context: Current matching uses address/size/rooms plus contact or image evidence, and special Morizon–Gratka/repost rules. Existing tests are useful but do not provide a labelled evaluation baseline. This task measures behavior; it must not weaken matching to make scores look better.
requirements: Create at least 200 labelled pairs: >=80 same-home, >=80 different-home and >=40 ambiguous/do-not-auto-merge. Labels must have a short rationale, scenario family and provenance; synthetic variations are not represented as 200 independently observed real cases.

Cover shared agency phone across multiple flats, building without unit number, different units/floors, stock/reused photos, resized URL variants, missing address/coordinates, same-price reposts, Morizon–Gratka shared IDs, conflicting cities and room/area boundaries.
Keep contact evidence synthetic/keyed and images local or synthetic URLs. Do not crawl/download private photos or use actual phone numbers for this dataset.
Split development and holdout scenario families with fixed IDs; prevent near-identical generated variants crossing the split. Freeze the holdout before T10 changes thresholds.
Output confusion counts, precision/recall on known labels, ambiguous auto-merge count and per-scenario failures. Treat ambiguous automatic merges as unsafe; report zero-division honestly.
Include an ingestion-level mode showing canonical counts and alert suppression on sequences, not only pair-function booleans. Save exact dataset hash, code SHA and parameters in the report.

acs.text: Dataset schema validates and each pair has a unique ID, label, rationale and scenario family.
Required pair counts and all scenario classes exist without private-data leakage.
Evaluation is deterministic and reports per-label/per-scenario results and failures.
Holdout families are separated and frozen before matcher tuning.
Sequence evaluation reveals both duplicate canonical homes and false same-home merges.

tasks.title: Expose bounded operational metrics and actionable local incident runbooks
tasks.goal: I want to know whether collection, indexing, alerts and account erasure are progressing, and how to diagnose failures without reading private listing or account content.
tasks.context: The existing API metrics endpoint exposes limited outbox information. Collection and delivery workers need consistent queue-age/failure signals. Metrics must remain internal and cheap to collect.
requirements: Publish queue depth and oldest eligible job age for search outbox, rental email, push and auth/erasure jobs from the service that owns the database. Define names, units, types and label allowlists in a metrics contract. Do not label by user, email, phone, listing ID, URL, request ID or arbitrary city text. Correlation IDs belong in redacted structured logs, not metric labels.

Make queue queries aggregate-only and indexed, with a bounded database timeout. A metrics collection error must not break ordinary user endpoints; expose collection failure separately. Do not claim process-local counters survive worker restarts or aggregate across replicas unless the implementation actually supports that.

Specify liveness as process responsiveness and readiness as ability to perform that service's required operations. Optional Elasticsearch fallback should not make the REST API unready when SQL discovery remains functional. Auth and delivery readiness must reflect their own essential dependencies without exposing passwords or full error strings.

Write runbooks for source 403/429, expired collection lease, old indexing revision, undelivered email, stalled account erasure and restore verification. Include read-only diagnostic commands, expected signals, safe retry conditions and escalation criteria; never automatically replay everything or send external incident messages.

Keep metrics and diagnostic routes off public ingress and deny unauthenticated internet access in config tests. Choose proposed alert thresholds (e.g. indexing age >5 min, eligible email age >15 min, erasure age >1 h) as explicit initial settings to calibrate using T07/T25, not proven SLA guarantees.
